content: Lamivudine and zidovudine can suppress your body’s ability to produce sufficient blood cells. Inform your doctor if you currently have or have ever had any blood-related conditions, such as anemia or bone marrow disorders. If you notice symptoms like unusual bleeding or bruising, shortness of breath, pale skin, fever, sore throat, chills, or other signs of infection, or if you feel unusually tired or weak, contact your doctor immediately. These medications may also lead to muscle-related disorders. Notify your doctor if you have a history of muscle diseases or muscle swelling. If you experience muscle pain or weakness, seek medical attention promptly. When taken alone or in combination with other antiretroviral drugs, lamivudine and zidovudine can cause severe liver damage and a potentially life-threatening condition called lactic acidosis. Inform your doctor if you consume or have consumed large amounts of alcohol or if you have a history of liver disease. Additionally, let your doctor and pharmacist know if you are taking acetaminophen (Tylenol) or if you have been on long-term HIV treatment. If you experience symptoms such as fatty or foul-smelling stools, nausea, extreme fatigue, unusual bleeding or bruising, lack of energy, loss of appetite, pain in the upper right abdomen, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or flu-like symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. It is essential to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and undergo any recommended laboratory tests. These tests are necessary to monitor your body’s response to lamivudine and zidovudine. The combination of lamivudine and zidovudine is prescribed to treat HIV infection in individuals with or without AIDS. These medications belong to a class of antiviral drugs known as synthetic nucleoside analogues, which work by slowing the spread of HIV in the body. However, they are not a cure for HIV and may not reduce the occurrence of HIV-related illnesses. Additionally, they do not prevent the transmission of HIV to others. Lamivudine and zidovudine are available as oral tablets, typically taken twice daily, with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more or less of the medication or alter the dosing schedule without your doctor’s approval. Even if you feel well, continue taking the medication as prescribed. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before starting lamivudine and zidovudine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to lamivudine, zidovudine, or any other medications. Be aware that lamivudine and zidovudine are also available individually under the brand names Epivir, Epivir HBV, and Retrovir, as well as in combination with abacavir under the brand name Trizivir. Inform your doctor if you are taking any of these medications to avoid duplicate therapy. Provide your doctor and pharmacist with a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Certain medications, such as acetaminophen, acyclovir, atovaquone, cancer chemotherapy drugs, cidofovir, dapsone, didanosine, doxorubicin, fluconazole, foscarnet, ganciclovir, interferons, methadone, nelfinavir, probenecid, ribavirin, rifabutin, rifampin, ritonavir, stavudine, trimethoprim, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, valproic acid, and zalcitabine, may require dose adjustments or careful monitoring for side effects when taken with lamivudine and zidovudine. In addition to the conditions mentioned earlier, inform your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Breastfeeding is not recommended while on lamivudine and zidovudine. Be aware that this medication may cause changes in body fat distribution, leading to increased fat in areas such as the breasts or upper back. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Lamivudine and zidovudine may cause side effects. Common side effects include headache, upset stomach, diarrhea, constipation, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty sleeping, excessive fatigue, depression, nasal congestion, cough, and hair loss. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects are rare but require immediate medical attention. These include hives, skin rash, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, seizures, numbness or tingling in the extremities, fever, or wheezing. If you experience any unusual symptoms or severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments while taking this medication. Inform laboratory personnel that you are using lamivudine and zidovudine before undergoing any tests. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
